whatThisIs: Three sources in this corpus are not exam papers but indices OF exam papers: a student-compiled list of what came up in each sitting, by round. They give no wording and no marks, so they cannot become questions. What they give is the one thing a single paper cannot — which topics recur, and in which round — so they are recorded here as exam-signal occurrences to be folded onto the concepts they name.

modelAnswers.title: HISTOLOGY MODEL ANSWER — ISK 101 (July 2023)
modelAnswers.whyThisMatters: The examiner's own model answer, with the marks allocated point by point and in halves. Every other mark scheme in this programme is authored from the department book and says so; this one is the department's. It should govern the two concepts it covers, and it shows the granularity the faculty marks at.

questions.asked: Describe the electron microscopic picture of rER.

modelAnswer.point: Continuous with the outer nuclear envelope
Covered with electron-dense particles, the ribosomes
Ribosomes bound to specific receptors (ribophorins) on the membranes by their large subunits
Under the receptor is a pore that allows newly synthesised proteins to enter
Proteins are stored in the rER cisternae

questions.asked: Determine the types of secondary lysosomes according to their content.

modelAnswer.point: Formed by fusion of a primary lysosome and a phagosome, or contains a phagosome or solid particles, or viruses and bacteria
Formed by fusion of a primary lysosome and a pinocytic vesicle, or has fluid content
Formed by fusion of a primary lysosome and an autophagic vesicle, or contains destroyed endogenous substance or a damaged organelle

modelAnswers.bearingOnExistingContent: Question 1b is the same objective as the concept `lysosome-types-electron-microscopy`, minted from the 2025 paper's Histology Q4. The model answer confirms the three types and, more usefully, shows that the faculty marks the name and the mechanism of formation as separate half-marks — so a mark scheme listing only the three names is worth half of what it should be. It also shows the accepted answers are alternatives joined by OR, which is to say the marking is open-set within each point.
modelAnswers.extraction: OCR, tesseract eng, --psm 4, single 1170x1208 image. Half-mark glyphs render inconsistently (as ½, ‘/2, %, 7 and ‘/) and were read as 0.5 throughout on the arithmetic: six points to three marks in each question.
